level_1: Identifies a patient’s problem with a potential toxicologic cause
level_2: Synthesizes all available data, including interview, physical examination findings, and preliminary laboratory data, to define the differential diagnosis
level_3: Modifies and refines evidence-based differential diagnosis based upon clinical course and data, and avoids premature closure
level_4: Recognizes toxicological presentations and/or conflicting diagnostic results that deviate from common patterns and require more complex decision-making
level_5: Develops guidelines, algorithms, or protocols used for education and guidance of learners, clinicians, or poison specialists

level_1: Orders diagnostic testing based on patient presentation
level_2: Interprets diagnostic testing in the evaluation of toxicologic disease
level_3: Orders advanced and ancillary diagnostic testing based on the pre- test probability of disease and the likelihood of test results altering management
level_4: Interprets advanced, ancillary, and forensic diagnostic testing
level_5: Develops and validates diagnostic testing processes or protocols

level_3: Formulates comprehensive treatment plans for patient’s with straightforward toxicologic conditions
level_4: Formulates comprehensive treatment plans for patient’s with complex toxicological conditions
level_5: Implements interdisciplinary team for patient’s with complex toxicological conditions

level_1: Recognizes substance use disorders (SUD) and withdrawal syndromes
Establishes a holistic treatment pathway involving institutional and community resources
level_2: Formulates treatment plan for patients with straightforward SUD and withdrawal syndromes
level_3: Initiates treatment of patients with complex
level_4: SUD and withdrawal syndromes
level_5: Selects therapies based on prior treatment response, co- morbidities, resources, and patient preference

level_1: Discusses basic concepts of biochemistry, physiology, and pharmacology
level_2: Describes basic toxicologic mechanisms and pathophysiology
level_3: Explains advanced toxicologic mechanisms and pathophysiology
level_4: Demonstrates knowledge of the mechanisms of complex and rare toxicological conditions
level_5: Demonstrates expertise through publishing or invited lectureship about toxicologic pathophysiology, and its epidemiologic associations

level_1: Identifies major routes of exposure among the human population [LN]
level_2: Identifies sources of environmental exposures to chemical, physical, and biological hazards for defined populations
level_3: Describes individual factors that impact susceptibility to adverse health effects from environmental exposures
level_4: Recommends methods of monitoring and reducing adverse environmental health effects for population
level_5: Uses data to characterize effects of exposure of a local population based on comparison with other populations

level_1: Selects ancillary testing needed to assess an acute exposure
level_2: Interprets the results of ancillary testing for an exposure incorporating the pharmacokinetics of the xenobiotic
level_3: Compares the analytical modalities, including appropriateness, limitations, and methodology
level_4: Demonstrates knowledge of advanced analytical and clinical testing, including alternative matrices
level_5: Develops protocols for advanced and alternative clinical testing

level_1: Discusses the relevant terminology of substance use, addiction, and withdrawal
level_2: Describes the biological basis, pharmacokinetics, and toxicokinetics of psychoactive and addictive substances
level_3: Explains the basis of treatments, both pharmacological and non- pharmacological, for patients with SUD and withdrawal
level_4: Identifies the systems- related issues that interfere with identification, analysis, and treatment of substance use and withdrawal
level_5: Develops protocols or curriculum for the management of patients with SUD or withdrawal

level_1: Identifies occupational hazards
level_2: Identifies relevant agencies and their role in risk assessment, mitigation, and education
level_3: Explains the core principles of occupational safety, risk assessment and communication, and hazard controls
level_4: Demonstrates the principles of occupational safety, risk assessment, and hazard control to patients or populations
level_5: Applies core principles of risk assessment and hierarchy of controls to reduce risks from safety hazards to patients or populations

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of common patient safety events
Participates in group disclosure of patient safety events to patients and patient families (simulated or actual)
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of how to report patient safety events
Conducts analysis of patient safety events and offers error prevention strategies (simulated or actual)
level_3: Identifies system factors that lead to patient safety events
Discloses patient safety events to patients and patient families (simulated or actual)
level_4: Reports patient safety events through institutional reporting systems (simulated or actual)
Actively engages teams and processes to modify systems for preventing patient safety events
level_5: Participates in analysis of patient safety events (simulated or actual)
Acts as a role model and/or mentor for others in the disclosing of patient safety events

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of basic quality improvement methodologies and metrics
level_2: Describes local quality improvement initiatives (e.g., consultation efficiency, testing turnaround times)
level_3: Participates in local quality improvement initiatives
level_4: Demonstrates the skills required for identifying, developing, implementing, and analyzing a quality improvement project
level_5: Creates, implements, and assesses quality improvement initiatives at the institutional or community level

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of care coordination
Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in complex clinical situations
level_2: Identifies key elements for safe and effective transitions of care and hand-offs
Role models effective coordination of patient- centered care among different disciplines and specialties
level_3: Coordinates care of patients in routine clinical situations effectively using the roles of the interprofessional team members
Role models and advocates for safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs
level_4: Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in routine clinical situations
Analyzes the process of care coordination and leads in the design and implementation of improvements
level_5: Coordinates care of patients in complex clinical situations effectively using the roles of their interprofessional team members
Improves quality of transitions of care within and across health care delivery systems to optimize patient outcomes

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of population and community health needs
level_2: Identifies specific population and community health needs for their local population
level_3: Uses local resources effectively to meet the needs of a patient population and community
level_4: Participates in changing and adapting practice to provide for the needs of specific populations
level_5: Leads innovations and advocates for populations and communities with specific health care needs

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Identifies key components of the complex health care system (e.g., hospital, skilled nursing facility, finance, personnel, technology)
Engages patients in shared decision making, informed by each patient’s payment model
level_2: Describes basic health payment systems (e.g., government, private, public, uninsured care), including practice models
Manages various components of the complex health care system to provide efficient and effective patient care and the transition of care
level_3: Describes how components of a complex health care system are interrelated, and how this impacts patient care
Advocates for patient care needs with consideration of the limitations of each patient’s payment model
level_4: Delivers care with consideration of each patient’s payment model (e.g., insurance type)
Advocates for or leads systems change that enhances high value, efficient, and effective patient care, and the transition of care
level_5: Discusses how individual practice affects the broader system (e.g., length of stay, readmission rates, clinical efficiency)
Participates in health policy advocacy activities

level_1: Demonstrates how to access and use available evidence and incorporate patient preferences and values to the care of a routine patient
level_2: Articulates clinical questions and considers patient preferences and values to guide evidence- based care
level_3: Locates and applies the best available evidence, integrated with patient preference, to the care of complex patients
level_4: Critically appraises and applies evidence even in the face of uncertainty and conflicting evidence to guide care, tailored to the individual patient
level_5: Coaches others to critically appraise and apply evidence for complex patients, and/or participates in the development of guidelines

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth

level_1: Demonstrates an openness to receiving performance data (feedback and other input)
Analyzes and reflects on the factors that contribute to gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
level_2: Demonstrates awareness that there may be gaps between expectations and actual performance
Using performance data, continually improves and measures the effectiveness of one’s personal and professional goals
level_3: Demonstrates an openness to receiving performance data and uses it to develop personal and professional goals
Analyzes, reflects on, and institutes behavioral change(s) to narrow the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
level_4: Identifies the factors that contribute to the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Acts as a role model for the development of personal and professional goals
level_5: Seeks and accepts performance data for developing personal and professional goals
Coaches others on reflective practice

level_1: Demonstrates professional behavior in routine situations and in reporting professionalism lapses
Analyzes complex situations using ethical principles, and recognizes the need to seek help in managing and resolving them
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of the ethical principles underlying patient care
Sets apart those situations that might trigger professionalism lapses and intervenes to prevent them in oneself and others
level_3: Identifies and describes potential triggers and takes responsibility for professionalism lapses
Uses appropriate resources for managing and resolving ethical dilemmas
level_4: Analyzes straightforward situations using ethical principles
Coaches others when their behavior fails to meet professional expectations
level_5: Exhibits professional behavior in complex and/or stressful situations
Identifies and addresses system-level factors that either induce or exacerbate ethical problems or impede their resolution

level_1: Takes responsibility for failure to complete tasks and responsibilities, identifies potential contributing factors, and describes strategies for ensuring timely task completion in the future
level_2: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in routine situations
level_3: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in complex or stressful situations
level_4: Recognizes situations that may impact others’ ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
level_5: Proactively develops and implements strategies to ensure that the needs of patients, teams, and systems are met

level_1: With assistance, recognizes the status of one’s personal and professional well-being
level_2: Independently recognizes the status of one’s personal and professional well-being and engages in help-seeking behaviors
level_3: With assistance, proposes a plan to optimize one’s personal and professional well- being
level_4: Independently develops a plan to optimize one’s personal and professional well-being
level_5: Coaches others when their emotional responses or level of knowledge/skills fail to meet professional expectations

level_1: Uses language and non- verbal behavior to reflect respect and establish rapport while accurately communicating one’s own role within the health care system
Organizes and initiates communication with a patient/patient’s family by clarifying expectations and verifying one’s understanding of the clinical situation
Independently recognizes biases of patients, while attempting to proactively minimize communication barriers
level_2: Identifies common barriers to effective communication (e.g., language, disability)
Establishes a therapeutic relationship in challenging patient encounters

Independently uses shared decision making with a patient/patient’s family to align their values, goals, and preferences with potential treatment options and ultimately to achieve a personalized care plan
level_3: With insight gained through an assessment of the patient’s/patient’s family’s expectations coupled with an understanding of their health status and treatment options, adjusts one’s communication strategies
When prompted, reflects on biases, while attempting to minimize communication barriers
Acts as a mentor to others in situational awareness and critical self-reflection with the aim of consistently developing positive therapeutic relationships and minimizing communication barriers
level_4: Establishes a therapeutic relationship in straightforward encounters with patients using active listening and clear language

With guidance, sensitively and compassionately delivers medical information to patients, elicits patient’s/patient’s family’s values, learns their goals and preferences, and acknowledges uncertainty and conflict
Develops educational programs or services that address bias or communication strategies.
level_5: Identifies complex barriers to effective communication (e.g., health literacy, cultural differences, technology)
Easily establishes therapeutic relationships with patients, regardless of the complexity of cases
Acts as a role model to exemplify shared decision making in communication with patients/patients’ families that embodies various degrees of uncertainty/conflict

level_1: Respectfully requests a consultation
Solicits feedback on performance as a member of the health care team
Uses effective communication to lead or manage health care teams
level_2: Uses language that reflects the values all members of the health care team
Integrates recommendations made by various members of the health care team to optimize patient care
Communicates feedback and constructive criticism to superiors
level_3: Receives feedback in a respectful manner
Engages in active listening to adapt to the communication styles of the team
Acts as a role model for communication skills necessary to lead or manage health care teams
level_4: Clearly and concisely requests a consultation or other resources for patient care
Communicates concerns and provides feedback to peers and learners
In complex situations, facilitates regular health care team-based feedback
level_5: Communicates information effectively with all health care team members
Acts as a role model for flexible communication strategies, i.e., those strategies that value input from all health care team members and that resolve conflict when needed

level_1: Accurately documents information in the patient’s record and safeguards the patient’s personal health information
Uses appropriate channels to offer clear and constructive suggestions for improving the system
level_2: Communicates through appropriate channels as required by institutional policy (e.g., patient safety reports, cell phone/pager use)
Communicates clearly, concisely, and contemporaneously in an organized written form, including anticipatory guidance
level_3: Demonstrates organized diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning through the patient record in a timely manner
Initiates difficult conversations with appropriate stakeholders to improve the system
level_4: Respectfully communicates concerns about the system
Models feedback to improve others’ written communication
level_5: Concisely reports diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning in the patient record
Facilitates dialogue regarding systems issues among larger community stakeholders (e.g., institution, the health care system, and/or the field)
